title: [P3] Generalise the lint rule `surfaces` axis to an open N-surface dimension (#4463 P1 introduced a closed two-value one)
body:
Restart-when: git grep -n "AUTHORING_SURFACES" -- packages/lint/src shows a proposed third value beyond cli / runtime-publish (growth in runtimeTypes does NOT restart it — that axis is already open, per #7220)

Split out of #4717 at dispatch, per the maintainer's 2026-08-07 migration ruling. Filed by the `domain:metadata` seat that landed the backend half; **unassigned, and deliberately carrying no `domain:*` label — routing is the triage seat's call** (this lands in `packages/lint`, not in `packages/metadata*`).

## What exists today

#4463 P1 introduced, **as needed rather than as a design**, a closed axis on lint rules:

- `surfaces: ('cli' | 'runtime-publish')[]`
- plus `runtimeTypes` and `surfaceReason`

That was not optional at the time and should not be read as speculative: it is the **structural precondition for the ratchet guard** — a guard cannot guard a surface that was never declared. So the axis earned its place; the question this card raises is only whether two values is the right arity.

## What this card asks

Generalise it to an open N-surface dimension, so a new enforcement surface is a declaration rather than an enum edit plus the guard changes that follow it.

## ⚠️ Grade this against the appetite bar before sizing it

Per the escalation guidance, an ability that no measured consumer is asking for is exactly what should **not** get built on speculation. So the first question for whoever takes this is not "how" but:

> **Is there a third surface actually arriving?** If the honest answer is "not yet", the correct outcome may be to hold this rather than build an open dimension for a set that has had two members since it was created.

Filing it because #4717's scope named it and dropping it silently would be worse than recording it — not because it is obviously due.

## The adjacent card that could supply the pull

**#7220** (`domain:spec-tooling`, currently `pm:blocked`) is the concrete instance of the same question from the other end: the four `views[]` visibility-predicate rules are **CLI-only**, so a Studio/REST/MCP `view` write bypasses all of them — and its own title records the constraint *"if they move to runtime-publish, they must move together"*. If those rules move, the axis gets exercised for real, and this card gains an evidence-backed reason to exist. Whoever grades this should read #7220 first; the two are likely one decision, not two.

## Related

#4463 (P1), PR #4715, #4717 (parent, now closed — its metadata half landed as `89d7b35a7`), #7220 (the CLI-only visibility predicates).
